To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stress in the myocardium is not only due to the LVP, but also depends on the stress generated by active fibers in the myocardium.
the intramyocardial stresses are very high and that their values are strongly dependent upon the depth of the measurement.
the intramyocardial stresses (IMS) are measured at the base and at the apex of the left ventricular free wall of isolated working and non working cat hearts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement and calculation of the intramyocardial stresses.
the measurement and calculation of the stress induced by active fibres in a passive medium, and the measurement and calculation the stress induced by LVP.
the development of a new technique of intramural pressure and stress measurement in the myocardium of isolated working and non-working hearts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the stress induced by a LVP is the sum of the stresses induced by the active fibers in the passive medium, the stresses induced by passive fibers in the passive and active media, the stresses induced in the passive media by the LVP, and the stresses induced by active fibers in the active media by the LPP.

, in the myocardium, the stress is the result of the interaction of three components, the stress induced by active fibers, the stress induced at the surface of the ventricle by the LVP, and the stress induced at a distance from the surface by the LVP.

, in the cat left ventricle, the stress in the passive medium (i.e. intramyocardial passive stress) is the major component of the intramyocardial total stress, and that the active component of intramyocardial stresses is negligible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stress generated by LVP is the sum of two components, one generated by the active fibers and the other generated by the passive medium of myocardium.
we were able to measure and calculate intramyocardial stresses at the base of left ventricles in working and nonworking isolated cat hearts, perfuse with Krebs-Hensleit buffer.

(1) the stress generated by active myocardial fibers in the direction of the LVP (S1) is equal to the product of the stress generated in the direction of contraction (S2) by a coefficient (α) that represents the ratio of the cross-sectional area of the active fibrous tissue to that of the whole myocardium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intramyocardial stresses are much higher than the stresses measured at the epicardium.
the stress generated by a fibre is proportional to the product of the fibre force and the fibre length.
the intramyocardial pressure (IMP) is a function of the intramyocardical stress (IMS).
